subject: [HelixHealth] Unexpected p99 spikes on 32k window requests - urgent
messages:
From: David Ruiz <david.ruiz@helixhealth.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: support@helixhealth.com
Date: 2028-06-15T09:12:00Z
Subject: p99 spike on 32k model requests - urgent

Hi Grace,

We're seeing sustained p99 latency increases for our nightly batch that uses the 32k window model (approx 2.4M tokens processed across ~600 requests in the 00:00-02:00 UTC window). Over the last 12 hours p99 went from ~1.8s to 9-12s and error rate increased to ~4% (timeouts). This is breaking our production pipelines and blocking diagnosis jobs.

Attaching a small CSV with request samples and timestamps. Can your team confirm this is related to the long-context path on the hosted API and advise on immediate mitigations? We need a fix or a temporary rollback/fallback today.

Thanks,
David
David Ruiz
Head of Machine Learning
HelixHealth

Attachments: helix_latency_summary_20280615.csv
From: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: david.ruiz@helixhealth.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-15T09:35:00Z
Subject: Re: p99 spike on 32k model requests - urgent

Hi David —

Thanks for the data and the heads up. I'm escalating to SRE and our inference leads; looping in Marissa and Rishi to investigate right away.

Immediate items we will start now:
- Marissa will pull the full traces and check queueing/batching behavior for 32k requests.
- Rishi will look at model variant routing and whether requests are being served by a slower quantized path.
- Laura will coordinate customer comms and provide status updates every 2 hours until resolved.

Do you have an ETA for when the next batch that hits the spike will run? If so, share (UTC) and we'll prioritize the preceding window.

— Grace
Grace O'Connor
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-15T10:02:00Z
Subject: Initial triage: 32k p99 spike (HelixHealth)

Team — quick summary from an initial probe (attaching sample heap/trace dump):
- Observation window: 2028-06-14 22:00 UTC -> 2028-06-15 08:00 UTC; p99 for 32k requests jumped from ~1.6s to 9-12s.
- Error rate rise correlates with increased KV cache misses for long prefixes and elevated kernel context-switching on a subset of hosts.
- Affected hosts: pool-hx-ld-07..09 (GPU models serving long windows); these hosts show a spike in CPU-side marshalling time, not GPU utilization.
- Spike coincides with a non-uniform request size distribution (a few very large 32k requests creating batch tail effects).

Immediate mitigations I recommend now (comfort-level: quick, medium, medium):
1) Route Helix 32k traffic to a warmed dedicated pool with conservative batching (route override) — quick.
2) Enable prefix-KV caching for Helix tenant on 32k model variant — medium, needs config push.
3) Temporal fallback: for requests with stable prefixes, route to 16k-quantized variant (fewer tokens) — medium, requires opt-in from Helix.

I've uploaded trace extracts and a ZIP of heapdumps to the Drive link and attached heapdumps_32k.zip.

I'll start a canary route to a warmed pool and post metrics in the ticket. If traffic persists we should consider a short-run autoscale bump for the ded. pool.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: heapdumps_32k.zip
From: david.ruiz@helixhealth.com <david.ruiz@helixhealth.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: alice.monroe@helixhealth.com, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-15T10:20:00Z
Subject: Re: p99 spike on 32k model requests - urgent

Thanks Marissa — that plan sounds reasonable.

Two notes:
- We can accept temporary routing to a warmed dedicated pool if it preserves correctness; we prefer it to a quantized fallback since accuracy of our post-processing is sensitive.
- Next Helix batch will run at 00:30 UTC tonight (2028-06-16 00:30 UTC). Can you confirm mitigations will be in place by then?

If you think we need to throttle something earlier, say so and we can update the job schedule.

— David
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, david.ruiz@helixhealth.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-15T13:08:00Z
Subject: Re: p99 spike on 32k model requests - urgent

David/Grace/Marissa —

Quick technical update after reviewing traces and kernel logs:
- The long-tail requests are causing a serialization backlog in the CPU pre/post-processing layer — some of our older host images have an inefficient I/O path for large KV pages.
- GPU device time remains within normal bounds; this is a software-side marshalling issue.

Planned actions:
A) Immediate (within 2 hours): switch Helix routing to a warmed dedicated pool (route override) to eliminate noisy multi-tenant interference.
B) Short (same day): push a config that lowers max-batch-size and enforces strict batch timeouts for their tenant on 32k variant.
C) Medium (48 hours): roll a lightweight patch to the host image to optimize KV page fetch and marshalling.

We'll schedule A+B ahead of their 00:30 UTC window and monitor p95/p99. Laura, can you confirm Helix accepts the dedicated-pool step? Grace, flagging for exec due to potential SLA impact.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Tech Lead, Inference Runtime
From: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: alice.monroe@helixhealth.com, david.ruiz@helixhealth.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-15T15:05:00Z
Subject: Exec update: HelixHealth production latency — immediate actions

Alice / David —

Quick executive summary and plan:
- Root cause (preliminary): CPU-side marshalling and KV miss amplification in long-context (32k) requests causing queueing at pre/post-processing layer, increasing p99 and error rate.
- Immediate mitigation: route Helix 32k traffic to warmed dedicated pool (scheduled now) and reduce per-tenant batching limits for 32k model.
- Risk: small increase in unit cost for dedicated capacity; we're prepared to absorb this for the next 72 hours while we stabilize.
- Next steps: patch to host image and follow-up postmortem by Monday.

Marissa and Rishi will execute A+B and confirm once the route is live. Laura will keep you updated every 2 hours until stabilization. If you'd like, we can set up a short executive call now (30 min) to align.

— Grace
Grace O'Connor
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Team / Helix —

Status update (post-mitigations):
- We routed Helix 32k traffic to a warmed dedicated pool and applied lowered batch-size + stricter timeouts at 2028-06-16 01:10 UTC.
- Result: p99 reduced from median 10.2s -> 1.9s within 45 minutes; error rate dropped below 0.3%.
- Follow-ups: Rishi will schedule the host-image marshalling patch (ETA 48 hours). Marissa will run a 72-hour soak and compile a postmortem.

Laura Bennett
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
